turn_text: Now, it seemed like you were kind of actively seeking to get on the Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry Committee. Was that one was real important to you?

It was really important to me to serve on the Agriculture Committee. And I'm really, so I did ask for that. And I'm really happy that I will have an opportunity to serve there. And the reason for that is that agriculture is, in my mind, really sort of the foundation of Minnesota's economy. And Minnesota farmers are not, if they're not having the easiest time right now with prices being low and record yields and then input costs being still pretty high, farmers are really struggling and having issues with working capital and small cash reserves. This year is going to be an important year for agriculture because we're riding a farm bill and I'm very happy I'll be able to bring the interest and concerns of Minnesota's ag community to this discussion in D.C.

Now you also were appointed to the health education labor and pensions. Now when you start talking about education of course in Minnesota that's also a really big issue. So what are your thoughts on that?

Well I'm really I also really wanted to be on that committee. And, you know, as Lieutenant Governor, I worked a lot on education and health issues. And I am especially hoping to, I especially plan to really push on issues having to do with childcare and really high quality childcare, which is a really important issue, certainly in all parts of the state. But I think most, a lot also in greater Minnesota where families sometimes have to drive a long way to get to their uh... to get a good child care option and then of course the health committee will also be uh... working on the opioid crisis which is just hitting minnesota so hard and i'm excited to be able to continue that fight and here in washington d c as well
well i know in rural areas of minnesota when you're talking about child care there's there's such a lack
and do you have ideas to bring to the table to kind of help with that. I mean you get kind of stuff rolling around in your head a little bit.

Yeah. Well, one of the big problems I think that we have in Greater Minnesota is that if you're wanting to have a child care, some sort of a child care or good quality daycare program, it's really hard to make the numbers work for a small business. You know, I understand this. I ran a small business. I had a small business. If you can't figure out how to make your income and expenses work, then it doesn't work. And one of the big problems is that the reimbursements for people who need help affording childcare are not what they should be. So that is one thing that I can help, I think, work on to make it a little bit more feasible for child care centers in greater minnesota to actually be able to operate
